Shentu Jia (申屠嘉 died 155 BC), posthumously known as Marquis Jie of Gu'an 故安節侯, was a native of Liang and a chancellor of the Western Han Dynasty.
Career
He started his career as a captain serving under Liu Bang, Emperor Gaozu of Han. He was made a Commandant (都尉) for his contribution in quelling Ying Bu's rebellion. During the reign of Emperor Hui, Shentu Jia was made the administrator of Huaiyang (淮陽守). In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, he was granted the rank of Secondary Marquis (關內侯) with a fief of 500 households worth of taxes. He was later made an Imperial Secretary (御史大夫). After chancellor Zhang Cang was dismissed, Emperor Wen lamented that many who followed Emperor Gaozu have already passed away and so Shentu Jia was made chancellor (丞相) and promoted to the Marquis of Gu'an (故安侯). He was known as an upright and uncorruptible official. During the reign of Emperor Jing, the Secretary Chao Cuo (晁錯) and Shentu Jia often disagreed on policy and the matter of the feudal princes. Shentu Jia accused Chao Cuo of a crime and requested his execution but the emperor pardoned Chao Cuo. Hearing of this, Shentu Jia regretted not killing Chao Cuo earlier and died from spitting blood. He was posthumously named Marquis Jie (節侯).
Family and Descendants
His son Shentu Mie (申屠蔑) succeeded him and was posthumously known as Marquis Gong (共侯). Shentu Mie's son Shentu Qubing (申屠去病) succeeded him. Shentu Qubing's son Shentu Yu (申屠臾) succeeded him and was stripped of his fief for accepting bribes when he was the administrator of Jiujiang Commandery (九江太守).
